channel_drafts.body:
Teaching exercise: Studio Riva and the assignment are fictional; the EDPB guide is an authentic public source.

For administration and customer service staff in small businesses in Italy. This information initiative helps organise the first steps after a request arrives. It does not announce a new law or decide an individual case.

**How do I recognise one?**
A person may ask whether you process personal data about them. They may also ask to access those data or receive a copy. These are elements of the access right described in the EDPB guide. If the request’s meaning is unclear, involve the person who handles privacy. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

**Who handles the response?**
The data controller must respond and facilitate the exercise of rights; the data processor assists the controller. As an organisational first step, refer the request to the person who handles privacy so they can check the business’s role and coordinate the response. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

**What should we record first?**
Suggested approach: retain the request and its receipt date, identify who is taking it forward, and record subsequent steps. The guide recommends internal procedures, staff training, knowledge of data flows and a record of requests and replies. This reminder does not replace your business’s procedure. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

**How much time is available?**
The guide states a response period of one month. If the request is too complex and more time is needed, the period may be extended by two further months, provided the person is informed within one month of receipt. Ask whoever coordinates the response to check the actual deadline and any extension; do not assume three months are always available. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

**Is sending a document enough?**
Access covers confirmation of processing and, where data are processed, access to the data and information such as purposes, categories, recipients and retention. The guide lists further required information. Before supplying a copy, check the rights and freedoms of others: a document may contain data about several people. Have the proposed disclosure reviewed before sending it. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

**Can we charge or refuse?**
A copy of the person’s own data is normally free. The guide describes particular conditions for additional copies or demonstrably manifestly unfounded or excessive requests. A repeated request should not automatically be refused. If a request is not granted, the person must be told within one month why, and about the possibility of complaining to the national authority and seeking a judicial remedy. Involve whoever handles privacy before deciding on fees or refusal. [European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

General information from the selected EDPB extract. The business’s role, data to disclose, actual deadline, possible fees and refusal grounds require individual assessment. No real request or business procedure is available.

channel_drafts.audience_note: For administration and customer service staff in small businesses in Italy. This information initiative helps organise the first steps after a request arrives. It does not announce a new law or decide an individual case.
channel_drafts.body:
Teaching exercise: Studio Riva and the assignment are fictional; the EDPB guide is an authentic public source.

“Receiving a personal data access request: six questions” is for administration and customer service staff in small businesses in Italy. Use the FAQ to recognise a request, record its receipt and involve the person who handles privacy.

Its guidance on response periods and checks before disclosure draws on the official EDPB guide. It helps organise the first steps; it does not replace your business’s procedure or assessment of an individual request. It does not announce a new obligation.

[European Data Protection Board (EDPB)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sme/be-compliant/respect-individuals-rights_en)

editorial_value.audience_value: The person receiving a message can identify what to flag, whom to involve and which decisions need review.
editorial_value.banality_check: Genericity is a risk; the six questions reduce it by connecting roles, records, timing and copy checks to a concrete task.
editorial_value.decision_enabled: It enables staff to organise a request and refer the relevant questions to the response coordinator, without deciding extensions, fees or refusal alone.
editorial_value.decision_limit: It cannot determine the answer owed to an individual or establish business compliance.
editorial_value.distinct_angle: The FAQ follows administration and customer service work from recognition to coordinated handling.
editorial_value.practical_use: It can serve as an initial reminder alongside the business’s procedure and its privacy contact.
editorial_value.publication_judgment: A useful proposal for internal review. The editorial recommendation does not authorise sending or publication.
editorial_value.reason_now: The firm has explicitly chosen to prepare staff for incoming requests; there is no new legislative event.
editorial_value.repetition_check: No previous communication was selected, so repetition and established house conventions cannot be assessed.
editorial_value.source_specific_information: The one-month period, conditional extension, controller/processor distinction and check on others’ rights give the communication source-specific substance.

voice.rhythm: Short sentences, one question per section.
